blocks.heading: Financial and non-financial rewards
blocks.text: Financial rewards are payments of money, such as wages, salary, bonuses or commission. Non-financial rewards include recognition, meaningful responsibility, development and benefits supplied as services rather than cash. A cash transport allowance remains financial even if it is called a benefit; an employer-provided transport service is a benefit in kind. Rewards can have different effects on staff according to their needs. Classify what is actually supplied rather than relying on the word allowance or benefit. Non-financial does not mean costless to the employer: providing transport, meals or developmental opportunities can use substantial resources.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Nara Foods pays a cash bonus and separately recognises a team’s achievement with greater responsibility. The bonus is financial; recognition and responsibility are non-financial. A worker who needs reliable income may not regard praise as an adequate substitute for wages.

blocks.heading: Financial rewards
blocks.text: Financial rewards are money payments received for work, including basic pay and cash incentives. They can meet living costs and provide a clear performance reward. Their effect depends on amount, fairness, reliability and what the employee values. A cash allowance remains a money reward even when intended to cover travel or housing. It differs from supplying the service itself.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Eya Works pays a cash travel allowance. The employee receives money, so it is financial. Calling it travel support does not convert it into praise, responsibility or a provided transport service.

blocks.heading: Non-financial rewards
blocks.text: Non-financial rewards provide benefits other than direct cash payments, such as recognition, achievement, meaningful responsibility, development or an employer-provided service. They may improve satisfaction and retention, but their relevance depends on staff needs and design. They can cost the employer money and do not remove its obligation to pay agreed wages. A cash bonus is financial even if labelled an appreciation benefit.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Olo Studio gives a capable designer responsibility for a complete project and acknowledges the result. Responsibility and recognition can provide satisfaction beyond basic pay. They are valuable only if the role has genuine authority and reasonable support.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain the reward classification: Luma Works pays a cash housing allowance to one worker and provides accommodation to another.

The allowance is financial because it is money paid to the worker. Providing accommodation is a benefit in kind, a non-monetary fringe benefit. Both can help housing needs and cost the employer resources, but their form differs. Calling the cash payment a benefit does not make it non-financial.
